title: Multi-language client transactional iterators and graceful degradation requirements
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Context: We need a cross-language spec and acceptance criteria for iterator-based client surfaces that support transactional pagination, robust retry/backoff semantics, and streaming reconnection with checkpointing. Goal is consistent developer ergonomics in Python/TypeScript/Go while preserving backward compatibility and allowing graceful client-driven degradation when server capabilities differ. This ticket produces the PRD and acceptance criteria for the SDKs team to implement adapters and runtime checks.
background: Customer signals: multiple customers building ingestion and long-running streaming consumers have hit issues around inconsistent cursor formats, opaque retry semantics, and poor reconnection behavior after transient network failures. Internal audits show duplicate efforts across language SDKs and high support volume around pagination edge cases. We want a single source-of-truth that SDK owners can implement with minimal per-language divergence.
goals: 1) Define a transactional iterator primitive for paginated endpoints: cursor semantics, resumability, and lightweight client checkpointing. 2) Define a streaming reconnect model with server-provided sequence tokens and client-side checkpoint persistence. 3) Standardize retry policies and idempotency guidance for mutate and non-mutating endpoints. 4) Provide a compatibility and deprecation matrix and adapter plan to ensure older SDKs degrade gracefully.
non_goals: Full client-side storage/sharding of checkpoints (only provide pluggable hooks and a reference filesystem/keystore adapter). Implement language runtime-specific memory optimizations (left to ENG runtime teams). Server-side guarantees beyond current best-effort ordering (no change to server SLOs).
requirements_clarifications:
- Cursor design: cursors must be opaque base64 strings with a documented stable prefix version token (e.g., 'rwd-v1:'). Clients must treat them as opaque but must include them in idempotency checks when resuming.
- Pagination modes: support both offset-like 'page' (for small datasets) and cursor-based streaming iterators; prefer cursor-based for production workloads.
- Transactional iterators: client exposes a pull API that returns pages plus a stable resume_token. On consumer checkpoint, SDK must be able to persist resume_token and later resume from that token with identical semantics.
- Streaming: server sends sequence numbers and periodic checkpoint markers. Clients may reconnect using last-seen sequence number or server-provided resume_token. SDKs must surface a reconnection hook and a pluggable checkpoint store interface.
- Retries: default SDK policy = exponential backoff with jitter; separate default policies for idempotent reads (aggressive) and non-idempotent writes (conservative + require user idempotency key). Timeouts: default per-request timeout 30s for control plane calls, streaming heartbeat 90s.
- Compatibility header: clients MUST send 'Rdw-Client-Version' and 'Rdw-Client-Feature-Flags' for feature negotiation. Servers will return 'Rdw-Server-Capabilities' with feature flags. SDKs must expose capability detection so app code can branch if server lacks a feature.
scope_changes: Initial scope (MVP): spec + SDK adapters + test harness. Excluded in MVP: persistent cross-process checkpoint storage adapters (we ship in separate follow-up), advanced prefetching heuristics, and automatic server-driven client fallback. During scoping review (2026-02-18) we dropped automatic persistent checkpoint sync to focus on clear API surface and local reference adapter.
acceptance_criteria: SDK surface parity: Python, TypeScript, and Go expose the same high-level iterator/stream primitives and feature negotiation hooks.

Interoperability test: a canonical end-to-end test harness can pause a consumer, persist a resume token, restart the client, and reconsumption resumes with no duplicate items (or clearly documented at-least-once semantics if server cannot guarantee).

Retry semantics: automated test validates default backoff for reads retries (min 100ms, max 10s, 5 attempts) and that write operations require explicit idempotency keys when using aggressive retry flag.

Compatibility detection: SDKs surface server capability map and provide a mechanism for developers to opt into graceful degradation paths; test verifies a client can detect a server lacking 'checkpoint-resume' and fall back to page-based iteration.
Docs & examples: each SDK repo has a README example for pagination checkpointing, streaming reconnect, and idempotent-write patterns.

Telemetry: SDK emits stable telemetry keys for 'resume_resume_token', 'stream_reconnect', 'retry_policy_used' and these map to console dashboards. Test verifies telemetry events emitted in sample harness.
implementation_notes:
- Design the checkpoint interface as a small trait/protocol with two methods: get(key)->string and put(key,value)->void; provide a local-file reference implementation in each language and a memory adapter for unit tests.
- Cursor encoding: server will include a versioned prefix; SDKs must never attempt to parse internals but may validate the version prefix and raise a descriptive error if unsupported.
- Backoff parameters should be configurable via SDK options and environment variables for rapid experimentation.
- Streaming reconnect: provide an exponential reconnect attempt with capped backoff and jitter; allow application callback to decide to drop/skip to latest.
- Compatibility headers to be added to all outgoing requests in the next API minor. Coordinate with API/Eng to ensure server includes Rdw-Server-Capabilities in responses.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Divergent per-language ergonomics cause support burden. Mitigation: provide canonical examples and shared e2e test harness. Risk: customers rely on implicit cursor stability. Mitigation: document that cursor format may change only with versioned prefix. Risk: reconnection semantics produce duplicates. Mitigation: provide clear docs and test harness demonstrating at-least-once vs at-most-once tradeoffs and recommend application-level dedup keys.

2026-02-18 // Scope review: Removed persistent cross-process checkpoint syncing from MVP to reduce scope; will ship reference adapters only.

2026-02-25 // Security review sync: No secret material in tokens; ensure persistence adapter uses KMS-backed storage when storing sensitive resume metadata. Security sign-off pending for KMS guidance.
2026-03-05 // SDK owners sync: TS owner raised backward-compat concern for existing cursor consumers; decision: add compatibility flag so SDK can opt into strict validation mode for early adopters.
progress_updates: 2026-01-22 // Initial draft PRD posted and shared with SDK owners.
2026-01-29 // Prototype checkpoint interface implemented in python-reference adapter (see GH PR #312).

2026-03-01 // TypeScript adapter draft done; awaiting Go implementation for parity.
2026-03-09 // QA smoke tests: basic pagination/resume passes; identified flakiness in heartbeat detection under heavy GC (Go); ENG investigating.
